questions.q: What does the CSA credential actually certify?
options: Baseline competence across the platform itself — navigation, users and groups, tables and fields, basic workflow configuration, and core ITSM processes
The ability to architect an entire multi-module ServiceNow program
Deep scripting and custom application development
Implementation of one specific product module such as ITSM or Discovery
questions.explain: CSA, Certified System Administrator, is the foundational credential covering baseline platform administration.

questions.q: Why does every CIS specialization list CSA as a prerequisite?
options: It's a licensing formality with no real connection to the exam content
Implementing any specific module depends on already understanding tables, roles, and configuration at the CSA level
CIS exams are administered by a different company than CSA
CSA is actually harder than any CIS specialization
questions.explain: The prerequisite reflects a real dependency: module-specific implementation skill builds directly on baseline administration skill.

questions.q: Past CSA, how should someone decide between branching toward CAD or toward a CIS specialization?
options: Flip a coin, since the two credentials are functionally identical
Always choose CAD, since development pays more in every case
Match the branch to the kind of work wanted — building new functionality points to CAD, implementing a specific module points to CIS — based on where real hands-on depth was built
Always choose CIS, since it is the only branch employers recognize
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as matching the credential to the actual work and actual hands-on depth built across courses 1-13, not a universal ranking.

questions.q: Why is CTA described as different from CSA, CAD, and CIS in this lesson?
options: CTA is actually easier to obtain than the other three
CTA has no connection at all to any of the skills built in this path
CTA is gated behind real, demonstrated implementation experience across multiple real projects, not simply passing another exam right after CAD or CIS
CTA is a renamed version of the CSA exam
questions.explain: CTA requires years of real project experience and the ability to defend architectural decisions — it isn't just 'the next cert' in sequence.

questions.q: Which courses in this path map most directly to the CAD credential's territory, per this lesson?
options: Platform Fundamentals and System Administration
Flow Designer, JavaScript for ServiceNow Developers, Scripting & Application Development, and IntegrationHub
CMDB, CSDM & Discovery only
Technical Architecture and the capstone
questions.explain: CAD certifies building custom applications — scripting, Flow Designer, scoping — which lines up with courses 4 through 7 of this path.
